title: Deploy in-cluster container registry
description:
Deploy a Docker registry (registry:2) in the `claude-workers` namespace for caching built devcontainer images.

Components:
- `registry/pvc.yaml` — 20Gi PVC using Longhorn StorageClass
- `registry/deployment.yaml` — registry:2 Deployment mounting the PVC at `/var/lib/registry`
- `registry/service.yaml` — ClusterIP service `registry` on port 5000

The full in-cluster hostname will be: `registry.claude-workers.svc.cluster.local:5000`

Resource limits: 200m CPU, 512Mi RAM (registry is mostly I/O bound).

Create a simple health check: `GET /v2/` should return 200.
acceptance_criteria: `kubectl apply -f agents/registry/` creates the Deployment, Service, and PVC
Registry pod is Running and healthy
`curl http://registry.claude-workers.svc.cluster.local:5000/v2/` returns HTTP 200 from within the cluster
PVC is bound to a Longhorn volume
Data persists across registry pod restarts

title: Configure K3s nodes for local registry
description:
Configure all three K3s nodes to trust and use the local in-cluster registry.

K3s uses `/etc/rancher/k3s/registries.yaml` on each node to configure registry mirrors and credentials.

Required config on each node:
```yaml
mirrors:
  "registry.claude-workers.svc.cluster.local:5000":
    endpoint:
      - "http://registry.claude-workers.svc.cluster.local:5000"
configs:
  "registry.claude-workers.svc.cluster.local:5000":
    tls:
      insecure_skip_verify: true
```

Create `agents/scripts/setup-registry-nodes.sh` that:
1. SSH into each node (beelink1/2/3 at 192.168.1.200-202 as user fox)
2. Writes the registries.yaml config
3. Restarts k3s (`sudo systemctl restart k3s`)
4. Waits for node to be Ready again

Note: Restarting k3s causes a brief workload disruption on that node. Script should restart one node at a time.
acceptance_criteria: `bash agents/scripts/setup-registry-nodes.sh` configures all 3 nodes
After running, K3s pods on all nodes can pull from the local registry
Test: push a small test image to the registry, create a pod that uses it, confirm it starts
Script is idempotent (safe to run again)
Script handles already-configured nodes gracefully

title: Create overlay Dockerfile
description:
Create `agents/base-image/overlay.Dockerfile` — a Dockerfile that layers Claude Code tooling on top of any project devcontainer image.

```dockerfile
ARG BASE_IMAGE
FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}

USER root

# Install Claude Code (skip if already installed)
RUN npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code 2>/dev/null || \
    (curl -fsSL https://nodejs.org/dist/v20.x/node-v20.x-linux-x64.tar.gz | \
     tar -xz -C /usr/local --strip-components=1 && \
     npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code)

# Install required tools if not present
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y tmux jq curl git \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* 2>/dev/null || true

# Install dotfiles
RUN git clone https://github.com/kfoxb/dotfiles /tmp/dotfiles \
    && cd /tmp/dotfiles && bash install.sh \
    && rm -rf /tmp/dotfiles

# Copy claude worker scripts
COPY entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh
COPY status-monitor.sh /usr/local/bin/status-monitor.sh
COPY hooks/ /root/.claude/hooks/

RUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/status-monitor.sh

ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh"]
```

The overlay is deliberately defensive — it handles cases where the base image already has Node.js or some tools installed.
acceptance_criteria: Overlay builds successfully on top of a minimal Ubuntu image
Overlay builds successfully on top of the existing homelab devcontainer image
Resulting image passes the same verification as the base image (claude, tmux, git, jq all work)
Build doesn't fail if base image already has Node.js or tmux installed
Image size is reasonable (documented in README)

title: Implement Kaniko build Job template
description:
Create `agents/build-job-template.yaml`, a Kubernetes Job template that builds a project devcontainer and applies the overlay using Kaniko.

The Job has two steps via init containers:

**Init container 1** (`clone`): Clone the target repo to a shared emptyDir volume:
```
git clone --depth=1 --branch $BUILD_REF $REPO_URL /workspace
```

**Init container 2** (`build-project`): Run Kaniko to build `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`:
```
kaniko --context=dir:///workspace \
       --dockerfile=/workspace/.devcontainer/Dockerfile \
       --destination=registry.../project-image:$PROJECT_HASH \
       --cache=true --cache-repo=registry.../cache
```

**Main container** (`build-overlay`): Run Kaniko to build the overlay:
```
kaniko --context=dir:///scripts \
       --dockerfile=/scripts/overlay.Dockerfile \
       --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=registry.../project-image:$PROJECT_HASH \
       --destination=registry.../project-image:$FINAL_TAG \
       --cache=true
```

Parameterized env vars: `REPO_URL`, `BUILD_REF`, `PROJECT_HASH`, `FINAL_TAG`, `REPO_SLUG`.

A ConfigMap mounts the overlay.Dockerfile and scripts into the build containers.

Resource limits: 2 CPU, 4Gi RAM (builds are CPU-intensive).
acceptance_criteria: `envsubst < agents/build-job-template.yaml | kubectl apply -f -` creates a build Job
Job successfully builds a real project devcontainer (test with a simple Node.js project)
Final image is available in the local registry
Build logs are readable via `kubectl logs`
Job cleans up (TTL after completion: 1 hour)
If project has no `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`, job handles it gracefully (exits with clear error)

title: Implement `ccw build` CLI subcommand
description:
Add `ccw build --repo <url> [--ref <branch/tag>]` to trigger and monitor image builds.

Flow:
1. Compute `PROJECT_HASH` from the Dockerfile contents:
   - Clone repo to a temp dir, hash `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`
   - Or use GitHub API to fetch file contents without cloning (faster)
2. Check if image already exists in local registry:
   `curl http://registry.../v2/<repo-slug>/manifests/<hash>` → 200 means cached
3. If cached: print `Using cached image: registry.../<slug>:<hash>` and exit
4. If not: create the Kaniko Job via `envsubst | kubectl apply`
5. Wait for Job completion: poll `kubectl get job <name>` every 10s
6. Stream logs: `kubectl logs -f -l job-name=<name> -c build-overlay`
7. On success: print final image tag
8. On failure: print error and logs

Also add `--no-cache` flag to force rebuild even if image exists.
acceptance_criteria: `ccw build --repo <url>` builds and caches an image for a repo with a devcontainer
Running `ccw build` a second time with same repo/hash uses cache (prints cached message, no Job created)
`ccw build --no-cache` triggers a rebuild regardless of cache
Build logs stream to terminal while Job runs
Printed image tag can be used in `ccw start --image <tag>`
Error if repo has no `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`

title: Integrate auto-build into `ccw start`
description: Update `ccw start` to automatically detect and use project-specific devcontainer images. Additional logic in `ccw start`: 1. If `--image ` is provided explicitly, use it (skip detection) 2. Otherwise: probe the repo for `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` using GitHub API: `curl -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \ https://api.github.com/repos///contents/.devcontainer/Dockerfile` 3. If found (HTTP 200): compute hash, check registry cache - Cached: use the cached image - Not cached: ask user "No cached image found. Build now? [Y/n]" (or `--auto-build` flag to skip prompt) - If yes: run `ccw build --repo ` inline, use result 4. If not found (HTTP 404): use the base `claude-worker` image This keeps `ccw start` fast in the common case (image already cached) while being helpful when a build is needed.
acceptance_criteria: `ccw start` on a repo with devcontainer uses the project-specific image (after building if needed)
`ccw start` on a repo without devcontainer uses base claude-worker image
With `--auto-build` flag, build happens without prompting
Cached image is used without rebuilding (fast path)
`ccw start --image <custom>` bypasses all detection
